transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… so, I’m here because this thing has gotten really bad for me at work. I’m a construction manager, so being around heights is not exactly optional, you know? But now, every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or one of those upper platforms, it’s like my head immediately tells me I’m about to go over the side.

And the frustrating part is I can see the rails are there. I can look right at the setup and know, logically, that it’s supposed to be safe, that it’s built the way it’s supposed to be built. I’m not looking at some flimsy thing and thinking, “Well, that’s dangerous.” It can be a proper scaffold, proper rails, everything in place, and still my mind just locks onto this idea that I’m going to fall. Like I’m about to tip over or get pulled over the edge somehow. It doesn’t match what I know, but it feels real in the moment.
Does this fear only happen when you’re up high or near an edge?

Yeah, it’s really tied to being up high or close to where there’s a drop. Like scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms—those are the big ones. It’s not just “being at work” in general. It’s when I’m near that edge or I have to step onto something elevated, and then my brain just jumps straight to, “You’re going to go over.”

And that’s what’s so strange about it, because I can be looking right at the guardrails, seeing that they’re there, knowing the setup is supposed to be safe, and it still doesn’t settle me. It’s like the height or the edge overrides everything I can see with my own eyes.
When you’re near a height or an edge, do you suddenly get a surge of intense panic?

Yes. It comes on really fast. It’s not like I stand there calmly thinking about it and then slowly get worked up. The second I step onto temporary stairs, or even just start walking toward an open upper floor, my body reacts before I can talk myself down.

My chest tightens up right away, and my hands get sweaty—like wet, not just a little nervous. And then I get this feeling in my legs like they’re going to lock up, like I might freeze before I can make myself take another step. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m standing there trying to look normal and keep moving, but inside it feels like my whole body is hitting the brakes.
Have you ever had one of these sudden panic episodes when you were not near a height or an edge?

I don’t think so… at least, not that I can clearly point to. The times I notice it are when there’s a height involved or I’m close to an edge, or even just heading toward one. That’s when it hits me in that sudden way.

I mean, I get stressed like anyone else, sure, but those full-on surges where my body just reacts immediately—those are tied to being up high or feeling like there’s a drop nearby. I haven’t really had that happen just sitting at home or driving or standing in a normal room, if that’s what you mean.
Do you avoid heights because of this fear?

Yeah, I do. More than I like to admit, honestly. I’ve started handing off a lot of the height-related inspections to my foremen—stuff I used to just do myself without thinking twice. If there’s a roof edge, an upper platform, anything like that, I’ll find a reason for one of them to go check it instead.

I’ve also been moving meetings to ground level whenever I can. Like if someone says, “Let’s walk it upstairs,” I’ll suggest we talk through it down below first, or I’ll say we can review photos or have someone bring the details to us. I make it sound practical, like I’m managing time or keeping things efficient, but really I’m trying not to go up there.

And when I absolutely have to go up, I don’t really do it alone anymore. I try to keep somebody right beside me, usually one of the foremen, and I get through it as fast as I can. I’m still scared the whole time, though. I’m not calm up there—I’m just rushing, trying to finish whatever needs to be done and get back down.
